mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with a housing rebound, which historically precedes a contraction in cyclical equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails to appear in at least two consecutive recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pressures firms' cost structures and compresses profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect inverts during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for four consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic activity that boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern fails during an inventory cycle peak.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over three months signals a deflationary monetary easing that increases risk aversion and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall > 0.5% over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 0.4% combined with a concurrent rise in Retail Sales (RSAFS) above its 3-month average signals robust household demand, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 70% of triggered months, or the pattern fails during a consumption-led bubble.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate earnings expectations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change < -0.4% in a single month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during a geopolitical shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in Industrial Production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity that reduces earnings visibility and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a supply-chain normalization.
